entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-crwc-vw2r-qr6m: OGNL stricter-invocation block list bypass via java.lang.reflect reflection proxies
entry.content:
OGNL stricter-invocation block list bypass via java.lang.reflect reflection proxies

Aliases: CVE-2026-113730

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L

Affected:

  • ognl:ognl — fixed in 3.4.13

### Summary OGNL's optional *stricter invocation* mode maintains a block list that prevents expressions from directly calling methods on dangerous classes such as `Runtime`, `ProcessBuilder`, and `ClassLoader`. The block list filters on the **declaring class of the method OGNL invokes**. Because `java.lang.reflect.Method` (and `Constructor`/`Field`) are not on the list, an expression can use reflection as a proxy — `someMethod.invoke(target, args)` — to reach a blocked method. The real call (e.g. `ProcessBuilder.start()`) then executes inside the JDK reflection machinery and never passes back through OGNL's `invokeMethod`, so the block list never sees it. ### Proof of concept Under the default OGNL context (public-only access, stricter invocation enabled), the following expression creat…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-9rhm-2h4x-jwmx: A2A Java SDK send client credentials under server-controlled HTTP header name, enabling leakage via redirect
entry.content:
A2A Java SDK send client credentials under server-controlled HTTP header name, enabling leakage via redirect

Aliases: CVE-2026-111763

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

*Impact.** A malicious or compromised A2A agent can cause the client's API key credential to be forwarded to an arbitrary third-party server. The agent serves an AgentCard with an `APIKeySecurityScheme` specifying a custom header name, then responds with an HTTP redirect. moquette is reachable by untrusted MQTT clients (anonymous by default), so every byte from any client, including pre-authentication, is untrusted. Audited at commit `da7f719a6bab9829d520b5838e13ea7b1f9be3ef`, module `broker/`. ## What a connecting client can do 1. (Critical) Bypass `pattern`-based ACLs across tenants. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-rxjv-24xq-76wc: JavaCV: Integer Overflow in IPCameraFrameGrabber Causes Infinite-Loop DoS
entry.content:
JavaCV: Integer Overflow in IPCameraFrameGrabber Causes Infinite-Loop DoS

Aliases: CVE-2026-102834

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.bytedeco:javacv — fixed in 1.5.14

### Summary `IPCameraFrameGrabber` parses the `Content-Length` value from the multipart MJPEG HTTP stream returned by the configured IP camera without any bounds checking. A malicious or compromised camera endpoint - or any network attacker able to tamper with the plaintext HTTP response (these streams are conventionally accessed over `http://`, as documented in the class itself) - can supply a `Content-Length` value in the range `1073741825`-`2147483647`. This drives the internal buffer-growth routine `ensureBufferCapacity(int)` into 32-bit signed integer overflow, which turns the "grow the buffer" loop into a true infinite loop: the loop variable oscillates to `0` and never again satisfies the loop's exit condition. The thread that called `grab()`/`grabBufferedImage()` spins at 100% CPU …

### Summary Junrar's RAR virtual machine can be forced into a deterministic infinite loop while extracting a crafted RAR4 archive. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-fp43-vj7g-pg92: OmniFaces: Forged combined-resource IDs and related output/push boundaries
entry.content:
OmniFaces: Forged combined-resource IDs and related output/push boundaries

Aliases: CVE-2026-102695

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.omnifaces:omnifaces — fixed in 1.14.3
  • org.omnifaces:omnifaces — fixed in 2.7.33
  • org.omnifaces:omnifaces — fixed in 3.14.23
  • org.omnifaces:omnifaces — fixed in 4.7.12
  • org.omnifaces:omnifaces — fixed in 5.4.2

## 1. Forged combined-resource IDs `CombinedResourceInfo` accepts a path-derived ID without an authenticity check, inflates it without an output limit, converts it to attacker-selected resource identifiers, and retains unique IDs in an unbounded static cache. In bounded tests, 20,754 encoded bytes inflated to 16,000,000 characters (about 770:1; about 49 MB observed heap delta), and 200 unique IDs added 200 permanent cache entries. A legitimately shaped short ID remained about 1:1, while malformed input was rejected; the missing distinction is between a server-issued ID and an attacker-minted but structurally valid ID. Affected:

  • io.openremote:openremote-manager — fixed in 1.24.2

### Summary A realm admin of tenant B can read the profile, client roles, and realm roles of any user in any other realm (including the master realm) by supplying the target user's UUID in the REST API path. Three read endpoints in UserResourceImpl check whether the caller holds the read:admin role but omit a check that the target user belongs to the caller's own realm. The vulnerability enables cross-tenant user enumeration and privilege-level reconnaissance. On a multi-tenant deployment the master realm administrator account is reachable from any tenant realm admin. ### Details The affected file is manager/src/main/java/org/openremote/manager/security/UserResourceImpl.java.
